To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a lack of software tools that can help in the evaluation of the usability of user-interfaces (UI), (2) the software tools that are available are not very user-friendly, and (3) the usability evaluation methods and techniques that have been proposed are not very well documented.

• The usability of a user interface can be evaluated by means of a set of techniques and tools, • These techniques can be grouped into four categories: inspection, testing, questionnaires and user observations, • The techniques can be used to evaluate a user interface at different levels of detail, • The techniques are complementary, • The evaluation process should be planned in a systematic way and should be based on a well-defined methodology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing software tools that can be used in the evaluation of user interfaces.
the development and application of a set of software tools for evaluating the usability of user interface design.
the development of a set of tools to support the evaluation process, and with the development of an evaluation methodology that will help the user interface designer to evaluate the user interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evaluation of user interfaces is a complex task that requires a multidisciplinary approach and a variety of different tools.
there is no single best technique to evaluate a user interface.
the software tools for evaluating the usability of UIs are not mature enough to be used by the majority of practitioners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to provide the user interface design community with a set of tools for evaluating and improving the usability of user interface designs.
it is possible to automate the evaluation of the usability of UI, but the current software tools are far from perfect.
we have developed a software tool for evaluating the usability of a user interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation process is not a trivial task, and it is important to understand the different methods and techniques that are available.

it is possible to use a software tool to evaluate usability, and that the use of such a tool is a very good alternative to the traditional methods of evaluation, which are based on the “craft” techniques.
it is possible to evaluate UIs in an objective manner using a software package.
